exposure: Standardized velocities of weight, length or height, and BMI gain in early infancy (0-0.5 years)
Growth periods (early infancy, late infancy, early childhood)
outcome: Time to Tanner pubic hair stage > 1
cohort: 7495 children from 36 cohorts participating in the Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes program
finding: Faster gains in weight, length/height, or BMI in early life were associated with earlier pubertal onset in both boys and girls.
mod_finding: This study did not examine the relationship between mode of delivery and pubertal onset, but it did find that children born to mothers who had a Cesarean section had faster gains in weight, length or height, or BMI in early life.
followup_time: Varies, until pubertal onset markers were reached
